sources.note: 27,136 bytes. The IAU constellation figures with name positions and some line modifications by the d3-celestial author (readme source note 3): one person's edits of the IAU figures, not an IAU product. Vertices are star positions at equinox J2000. 89 features (Serpens twice), GeoJSON MultiLineString, longitude -180 to 180. Repository: https://github.com/ofrohn/d3-celestial.

sources.citation: Davenhall, A. C. and Leggett, S. K. (1989), Catalogue of Constellation Boundary Data, VizieR catalogue VI/49.
sources.note: 40,714 bytes. Davenhall and Leggett (1989), Catalogue of Constellation Boundary Data, VizieR VI/49 (readme source note 4): the Delporte boundaries the IAU adopted, drawn at equinox B1875. Vertices here are their J2000 positions; each edge follows a constant B1875 right ascension or declination. 89 closed Polygon rings. Repository: https://github.com/ofrohn/d3-celestial.

files.note: All 89 constellation figures, evidenceKind 'catalog-derived': the IAU figures as edited by the d3-celestial author, not an IAU product. Changed from the source: right ascension wrapped from -180..180 into 0..360 at 4 decimals, rank as an integer, the two Serpens features named Se1 (Caput) and Se2 (Cauda) by right ascension; nothing else.

All 89 IAU constellation boundaries, evidenceKind 'catalog-derived'. Vertices are J2000 positions of B1875 corners; each edge follows a constant B1875 right ascension or declination, so a layer must densify edges along B1875 right ascension or declination, never draw them straight. Changed from the source: right ascension wrapped from -180..180 into 0..360 at 4 decimals, rank as an integer, the two Serpens features named Se1 (Caput) and Se2 (Cauda) by right ascension; nothing else.
